EA-08.name: Maintained technical changeability
EA-08.original_form: Refactoring, simple design, collective ownership and technical debt control.
EA-08.mechanism: Continuously restructure behaviour-preservingly, remove friction and budget deliberate debt repayment.
EA-08.mature_form: Preserve the options that future evidence is likely to require.
EA-08.trigger: The system is expected to evolve and internal quality is slowing safe change.
EA-08.native_cheap_path: For a disposable prototype or imminently retired component, isolate or replace rather than perfect it.
EA-08.ceremony_distinction: A refactoring sprint or debt backlog is optional and can itself become theatre.
EA-08.criticism: Refactoring benefits are difficult to isolate empirically; short-term feature incentives can suppress it.

EL-040.name: Immutable standardisation and procedure compliance
EL-040.original_form: Define one best way and require conformance.
EL-040.mechanism: Central authors prescribe and audit compliance; deviations are treated as worker failure.
EL-040.mature_form: No immutable general standard; use risk-calibrated constraints within a versioned and reviewable baseline.
EL-040.trigger: NO GENERAL TRIGGER. Safety-critical immutable constraints may exist, but even they require controlled review.
EL-040.native_cheap_path: Use EL-017: a current baseline with explicit exceptions, change rights and review.
EL-040.ceremony_distinction: Standard-work sheets, SOP audits and conformance scores are not proof of capability.
EL-040.criticism: Worker studies link workflow formalisation and autonomy loss to poorer outcomes; mature Lean interpretations describe standards as improvable baselines.
